title: Supply concerns drive FAO Food Price Index higher
key_claim: FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.3 points in August 2026, up 1.9 percent from July and 2.5 percent year-on-year; the cereal index rose 2.2 percent m/m (wheat +2.6 percent, +15.0 percent y/y); the sugar index rose 11.9 percent.
frame_summary: FAO frames the August rise as converging supply shocks and geopolitical trade disruption tightening supply expectations, not a demand story.

title: Ukrainian Strikes Halt Most Russian Grain Exports in the Black Sea
key_claim: More than 90 percent of Russia's Azov-Black Sea grain export capacity was shut after Ukrainian strikes; all three Novorossiysk grain terminals suspended operations, a basin that normally handles 88 percent of Russia's maritime grain shipments and about 15 billion dollars a year in revenue.
frame_summary: The Moscow Times frames the strikes as a major supply shock that has not yet broken prices, since markets are still betting on ample global supply rather than panic.
cluster: Grain and water systems buckle under compound stress
verbatim_quote: Grain exports bring around $15 billion into the Russian economy annually, while the Azov-Black Sea basin accounted for 88% of Russia's maritime grain shipments last season.

title: Russia Zeroes Out Grain Export Duties as Black Sea Attacks Choke Shipping
key_claim: Russia eliminated export duties on wheat, corn and barley through the end of 2026 (wheat duty had been 787.5 rubles per tonne) after repeated Ukrainian strikes on Black Sea port infrastructure; alternate routes can absorb only hundreds of thousands of extra tonnes a month, far below normal Azov-Black Sea capacity of over five million tonnes.
frame_summary: Global Agriculture frames the duty suspension as a modest palliative that cannot offset a physical shipping bottleneck, with security risk still destabilising freight and insurance markets.
cluster: Grain and water systems buckle under compound stress
verbatim_quote: Russia has eliminated export duties on wheat, corn and barley for the rest of 2026, a move Moscow says is meant to support exporters after repeated Ukrainian strikes on Black Sea port infrastructure left grain shippers struggling to move the new harvest out of the country.

title: India Lifts Wheat Export Ban to Ease Global Supply
key_claim: India's Directorate General of Foreign Trade lifted its 2022 wheat export ban entirely on 24 August 2026, after a partial 2.5 million tonne quota easing in February; record 2025-26 food-grain output of 376.563 million tonnes (+5.3 percent y/y) and record wheat output of 120.657 million tonnes underpin the move, with Chicago wheat futures having climbed more than 17 percent between July and late August on Black Sea disruption.
frame_summary: Supply Chain Digital frames India's move as a supply-side relief valve for global markets strained by Black Sea disruption, enabled by India's own record harvest.

title: Fair summer crop yields expected in Ukraine
key_claim: Ukraine's 2026 summer crop yields are regionally mixed: western drought and central rainfall deficits cut potential while eastern regions saw fair-to-positive conditions; grain maize forecast at 7.40 t/ha (35.1m t), sunflower 2.29 t/ha (14.0m t), soybean 5 percent below average at 3.68m t (23 percent below the five-year average).
frame_summary: JRC frames Ukraine's 2026 harvest as regionally divergent rather than uniformly poor, cautioning against reading the drought narrative as universal.
cluster: Grain and water systems buckle under compound stress
verbatim_quote: Persistent drought in western regions and rainfall deficits in parts of the centre reduced yield potential, while timely rainfall and the absence of severe thermal stress supported fair to positive conditions elsewhere.

title: El Nino Pushes Cocoa Prices Higher as West Africa Supply Risks Return
key_claim: Cocoa hit six-month highs on 9 July 2026 amid a forming El Nino threatening West African output; Cote d'Ivoire's crop is forecast to fall to 1.7-1.8 million tonnes versus roughly 2.2 million tonnes in 2025/26, with West Africa supplying more than 60 percent of global cocoa.
frame_summary: Ecofin Agency frames the cocoa price rise as an early warning of a fresh El Nino-driven West African supply shock layered on the still-unresolved cocoa crisis.

title: EU officially adopts 2040 climate target, postpones ETS 2 by one year
date_evidence: updated on March 10, 2026; "On 5 March 2026, the EU Council formally adopted amendments to the European Climate Law"
